heading: Stock Market Highlights Today: Nifty Ends Above 23,400, Sensex Closes 560 Points Higher
paragraphs: The Nifty 50 settled 67.90 points higher at 23,414.30, compared with its provisional close of 23,429. The Sensex settled 564.03 points, or 0.76%, higher at 74,858.99, compared with its provisional close of 74,894.86. That came amid higher US equity futures, as investors assessed the outlook for US-China trade ahead of a planned summit later this week.
The planned meeting between the US and China remained a key focus for investors, who were watching for signs of progress in trade discussions between the two countries.

US stock futures were also higher in early trading. S&P 500 futures gained 0.23%, Nasdaq-100 futures rose 0.27% and Dow futures added 0.25%. The moves followed a third straight weekly decline for the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

The market moves came after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates last week, marking its first rate hike in three years. Persistent inflation remained a concern for policymakers, while rising bond yields continued to weigh on financial markets.
The 10-year US Treasury yield was around 5%, while crude prices stayed close to the $100-a-barrel mark.

Oil prices were broadly stable as traders assessed the potential impact of Middle East supply risks against diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran conflict. Brent crude was near $104 a barrel after falling for three consecutive sessions, while West Texas Intermediate remained below $100.
The Nifty 50 settled 67.90 points higher at 23,414.30, compared with its provisional close of 23,429.
The Sensex settled 564.03 points, or 0.76%, higher at 74,858.99, compared with its provisional close of 74,894.86.
The Nifty 50 provisionally closed 82.60 points higher at 23,429. The Sensex gained 599.90 points, or 0.81%, to 74,894.86.
The Mumbai, Thane, Raigad and Palghar Petrol Dealers Association has asked the RBI to exempt fuel retailers from UPI merchant discount rate charges, according to a letter sent to the regulator.

The association warned that petrol pumps across Mumbai could stop accepting UPI payments from Oct. 15 if the charges are imposed. Dealers said regulated fuel prices prevent them from passing transaction costs to consumers.
Deepak Fertilisers rose 1.80%, while JG Chemicals gained 1.11%. UPL fell 3.09%, while Thirumalai Chemicals declined 1.17%.
Voltas rose 2.85%, while Indian Hotels gained 2.12%. TCS and Tata Consumer Products advanced 1.45% and 1.24%, respectively.
Nelco fell 2.54%, while Tata Investment Corporation and Tata Power declined 2.53% and 2.03%, respectively.
Arfin India rose 1.54%, while National Aluminium Company gained 1.03%. Maan Aluminium and Hindalco Industries advanced 0.74% and 0.70%, respectively.
Vedanta Aluminium slipped 0.14%, while Manaksia Aluminium declined 0.11%.
The rupee strengthened 0.1% to 95.80 against the US dollar, compared with Friday’s close of 95.87.
Brent crude declined 2.4% to $101.47 a barrel.
Renaissance Global rose 5.12%, while Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri gained 5%. KDDL advanced 3.41%, while PC Jeweller and Titan Company rose 2.20% and 1.29%, respectively.
Thangamayil Jewellery fell 2.71%, while Motisons and Senco Gold declined 1.31% and 1.29%, respectively.

Tata Steel MD and CEO TV Narendran said coking coal prices have risen by $60 and account for about 40% of steelmakers’ costs. Steel companies are raising prices in anticipation of the impact over the next two months.
Narendran said zinc, aluminium, copper and manganese prices have also increased. Tata Steel did not provide margin guidance.
Nifty Realty rose 1.37%, while Nifty FMCG gained 1.29%. Nifty Pharma and Defence advanced 1.17% and 0.81%, respectively.
Nifty Metal fell 0.43%, while Nifty Rural and PSU Bank declined 0.10% and 0.01%, respectively.
The Nifty 50 rose 109.15 points to 23,455.55. The Sensex gained 659.98 points, or 0.89%, to 74,954.94.

Marine Electricals opened a plant in Goa to expand its manufacturing and operational capacity. The facility will focus on power train units for data centres and shore conversion systems for ports, according to an exchange filing.

Microsoft formally launched its India South Central cloud region in Hyderabad as part of its $20.5 billion investment commitment towards India’s digital and artificial intelligence infrastructure, PTI reported.
The region joins Microsoft’s existing cloud regions in Pune, Chennai and Mumbai. The Hyderabad facility uses air-cooled chillers and requires no water for cooling.
India Pesticides expects revenue to grow nearly 15% and EBITDA margin to remain at 15–16%. The company said customers had agreed to a price increase.
Exports are expected to contribute 40–45% of revenue. New products could generate Rs 25–30 crore in their first year, with business in new areas expected to begin within three months.

SpiceJet has delayed or cancelled several flights in recent weeks and has yet to pay salaries for the past three-and-a-half months, according to sources. The airline is operating 11 aircraft and is considering fundraising options.

SpiceJet is awaiting Rs 350 crore under the ECLGS 5.0 scheme. Operations are expected to improve from mid-October with the induction of 20 wet-leased aircraft. NDTV Profit is awaiting a response from the airline.
Kirloskar Ferrous Industries appointed Ankur Gupta as deputy chief financial officer, effective October 1.
The company also appointed Ajay Shriram Pati as joint managing director for three years, effective September 21, according to an exchange filing.
GK Energy received a letter of award from Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company to set up a 150 MW/300 MWh battery energy storage system in Maharashtra.
The company will receive a tariff of Rs 2.38 lakh per MW per month under the project, according to an exchange filing.
Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran said major agencies expect India to grow 6–6.5% annually over the medium term.
Speaking at an AIMA event, Nageswaran said the economy grew 7.8% in the first quarter despite the West Asia crisis. He attributed the growth to reforms implemented over the past decade.
Shriram Finance’s board approved the purchase of notes worth up to $460 million issued under its Global Medium Term Note programme, according to an exchange filing.
IIFL Finance approved the allotment of non-convertible debentures worth Rs 130 crore, according to an exchange filing.

Sonaselection India’s IPO was subscribed 1.36 times as of 12:27 pm on the final day of bidding. The retail portion was subscribed 1.91 times, while the non-institutional investor segment was booked 1.30 times.
The qualified institutional buyer portion was subscribed 0.46 times.

The NSE IPO was subscribed 1.82 times as of 11:57 am on the final day of bidding. The non-institutional investor portion was subscribed 3.04 times, while the qualified institutional buyer segment was booked 2.42 times.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it would deploy weapons with new capabilities and target new locations if the US launched another attack, Al Jazeera reported.
IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi said Iran would also change the geographical scope of its defensive and counteroffensive operations.
The US FDA issued five observations under Form 483 after inspecting Cohance Lifesciences’ Andhra Pradesh facility from September 14 to 19, according to an exchange filing.
India and Bangladesh are discussing the formation of a joint task force to expand bilateral trade and investment, PTI reported.
The proposed panel would bring businesses and other stakeholders from both countries together and work towards removing tariff and non-tariff barriers.
Piramal Finance will allot non-convertible debentures worth Rs 1,100 crore through a private placement, according to an exchange filing.

GlassRatner Advisory’s Seth R. Freeman said 10-year bond yields were attractive for investors. Freeman added that it remained unclear whether companies were passing on the full increase in commodity costs.

Helios Capital’s Dinshaw Irani said a prolonged war could weigh on second-quarter earnings, while an early end could support results. He expects crude oil prices to decline and remains positive on the BFSI sector despite pressure on banks’ current and savings account deposits.
Irani said large-cap valuations were not a concern for foreign portfolio flows, but saw limited room for growth among large-cap stocks.
Former HPCL CMD M.K. Surana said crude supply concerns could intensify if the US imposes tariffs under the Russia sanctions bill.
Surana said the law gives the US president authority to act, but markets do not expect immediate implementation. He added that estimating India’s actual crude oil cost remains difficult.
ICICI Securities’ Probal Sen said uncertainty around oil marketing companies could continue until the war ends.
Sen identified Oil India and ONGC as his top picks in the oil and energy sector, adding that energy security remains a priority for the Indian government.
Puravankara plans to launch a project with about 2,200 units in Kerala, Mallanna Sasalu said. The company has a presence in Chennai and Kochi.
Pre-sales at its new Bengaluru project stand at Rs 1,000 crore. The project is expected to be completed in the next two-and-a-half years.
Kaynes Semiconductor’s Raghu Panicker said low-volume production has begun, with full production scheduled to start in December. The unit can produce 1.2 billion devices annually.
Panicker expects 80–90% of the semiconductor capacity to be utilised soon. The products can be used in industrial air conditioners and washing machines.
The Nifty 50 rose 19.65 points, or 0.08%, to 23,366.05. The Sensex gained 339.14 points, or 0.46%, to 74,634.10.

NaBFID plans to raise $500 million through a 10-year overseas bond and is in talks for a $1 billion bond backed by the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency with a 15-year maturity, The Economic Times reported.
The development finance institution plans to use the funds for long-term infrastructure financing, the report said.
Manika Plastech discovered its listing price at Rs 43 on the NSE and BSE, unchanged from its issue price.
SAIL raised blended product prices by 3–5%, effective September 19, according to NDTV Profit’s channel checks. Prices of 8 mm and 10 mm products increased by Rs 1,000–3,000 per tonne.
SAIL shares traded 0.41% higher at Rs 178.05 after touching an intraday high of Rs 179.80.
Lenskart shares fell 2.09% to Rs 692.45 after 3.53 crore shares changed hands in a block trade, representing 2% of the company’s equity.
The stock traded between Rs 683 and Rs 698.30 during the session.
Oracle Financial Services Software fell 3.13%, while Coforge and Wipro declined 2.61% and 2.06%, respectively. Newgen Software and Infosys lost 1.78% and 1.76%.
Tata Elxsi rose 0.32%, while Latent View Analytics gained 0.08%.
The Nifty 50 fell 2.80 points, or 0.01%, to 23,343.60 at the opening bell. The Sensex rose 260.69 points, or 0.35%, to 74,555.65.
Several large-cap stocks enter the session with fresh brokerage commentary on execution, demand, competition and growth.

Hindustan Aeronautics has Buy or Outperform ratings from Goldman Sachs, Citi and CLSA, while Morgan Stanley retains an Overweight rating on Polycab India. Jefferies maintains Buy ratings on IndiGo, Grasim Industries, Titagarh Rail Systems and JSW Infrastructure.
Indian semiconductor companies are in focus after JPMorgan highlighted developments around domestic chip production and the potential expansion of OSAT capacity.

JPMorgan said Kaynes is planning a $1 billion OSAT investment under ISM 2.0, while Kaynes, CG Power, Micron, CDIL and Suchi Semicon are exporting chips and supplying them domestically. The brokerage said clients are booking chips amid high demand, with companies focused on ramping up production.
Jefferies has maintained its Buy rating on JSW Infrastructure, citing planned capacity additions across ports and logistics.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 395 • Management reiterated its target to double EBITDA over FY26-28E. • Growth is expected to be led by ports and logistics capacity additions. • Capacity addition targeted at 61% in FY27 versus FY26. • The company targets a 2.2x capacity increase over FY26-30 to 400 MTPA by FY30E. • Logistics expansion is gaining traction through terminal and rake additions. • Jefferies sees 25% FY26-30E EBITDA CAGR visibility.
Jefferies has highlighted stronger hotel industry operating trends, with August RevPAR growth supported by rates and occupancy.

• Hotel industry RevPAR rose 18% in August. • Growth was driven by stronger rates and occupancy. • Metro markets outperformed leisure destinations in August. • September demand has been supported by large MICE events. • Jefferies expects a strong finish to the second quarter of FY27. • Hotels in its coverage universe are expected to deliver EBITDA CAGR of around 12-19% over FY26-29E.
Jefferies expects Titagarh Rail Systems to benefit from passenger rail expansion and higher execution.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 990 • Management remains confident of scaling the passenger rail business over FY26-30E. • Growth is expected to be driven by the order book, execution pickup and railway modernisation plans. • Freight Rail Services should remain steady, with potential order inflows in FY27E. • The recent MoU with Siemens supports opportunities in international metro stock. • Jefferies estimates 44% FY26-30 EPS CAGR led by the passenger rail order book.
The Nifty 50 fell 15.95 points, or 0.07%, to 23,330.45. The Sensex rose 241.83 points, or 0.33%, to 74,356.79.
Jefferies has retained its Buy rating on Grasim after discussions at the Jefferies India Forum 2026.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 3,910 • Opus Paints targets more than 50% growth in FY27. • The paint business targets profitability by the end of FY28. • VSF profitability is supported by healthy industry demand. • Birla Pivot targets EBITDA breakeven by the end of FY27. • The renewable business is scaling rapidly. • Net debt-to-EBITDA is targeted below 2x.
JPMorgan has highlighted potential capacity expansion in India's semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem following the India Semiconductor event.

• Kaynes is planning a $1 billion OSAT investment under ISM 2.0. • The proposed investment would be three times its ISM 1.0 commitment. • JPMorgan flagged a potential announcement from Kaynes on its OSAT application. • Kaynes, CG Power, Micron, CDIL and Suchi Semicon are exporting chips and supplying them domestically. • Chips are being booked by clients amid high demand. • The focus remains on ramping up production.
CLSA has retained an Outperform rating on Nestle India while highlighting regulatory action involving infant nutrition products.

• Rating: Outperform • FSSAI has initiated regulatory action concerning infant nutrition products. • Claims related to HMOs and digestibility are under scrutiny. • Three separate adjudication cases have been filed against the company. • Milk products and nutrition contribute one-third of sales. • The nutrition segment contributes a higher share of profitability.
UBS expects Shaily Engineering Plastics to benefit from Sandoz's approval to launch generic semaglutide in Canada.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 4,500 • Sandoz received approval to launch generic semaglutide in Canada. • The product will be launched in three strength doses through a pen format. • The development is positive for Shaily given its dominant share of the Canadian pen market. • UBS estimates 40 million pens versus guidance of 36 million.
Morgan Stanley expects Polycab's distribution network and scale to remain important as new competition enters the cable market.

• Rating: Overweight • Target price: Rs 10,545 • Polycab is preparing for the entry of new cable brand Ultravolt. • The brokerage expects a larger impact on smaller unorganised players. • Around 30-35% of wires remain unorganised versus around 10% in cables. • Ultravolt's initial capex of around Rs 18 billion is modest relative to Polycab's existing scale. • Polycab has around 10,000 cable SKUs. • Distribution and supply chain remain key strengths, with the ability to service customers within around 24 hours.
HSBC expects UltraTech Cement's volume growth and profitability to remain supported by its scale and pricing.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 14,200 • Industry-leading profitability and volume growth are expected to continue. • Cement price increases in September are likely to offset the variable cost increase. • HSBC disagrees with concerns around profitability versus market share. • India presence, size and scale should support valuation premiums. • One-year forward EV/EBITDA has declined from 26x at its peak to 13.7x currently. • UltraTech has consistently grown faster than the industry, and HSBC expects this trend to continue.
Jefferies expects IndiGo's near-term industry environment to remain focused on profitability, while retaining its positive view on the airline.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 5,840 • Management highlighted near-term industry rationalisation. • Airlines are prioritising profitability over growth amid elevated costs. • Pricing and yields remain strong. • Capacity growth is expected to remain flattish year on year in the second quarter. • PRASK guidance of around 25% remains unchanged. • Management sees recent fare hikes as partly sticky. • Cost actions and the management transition remain on track. • Strong balance sheet supports IndiGo's FY30 growth ambitions.
The rupee opened at 95.81 against the US dollar, compared with Friday’s close of 95.87.
UBS expects leadership clarity and improving loan growth to remain key factors for HDFC Bank.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 1,000 • CEO names have already been submitted to RBI, with clarity expected soon. • Loan growth showed early recovery at 15.6% in Q1FY27. • Loan growth is expected to improve towards 15% over FY27-29E. • Margins are expected to improve towards 3.5%, aided by a shift towards retail loans. • RoA is seen improving to 1.9% in FY27/28E. • Deposit CAGR is forecast at 15.5% over FY26-28E. • 42% of branches are less than five years old.
JPMorgan has retained its positive stance on Tata Capital, highlighting NIM improvement and maintaining its growth outlook.

• Rating: Overweight • Target price: Rs 395 • NIM improvement remains a key strategic priority. • Growth guidance remains intact at 23-25%. • Asset quality remains benign despite macro headwinds. • Flexi-book remains in focus, with net exposure below 5%. • FCNR impact is nuanced.
MOSL has initiated coverage on Pine Labs with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 250, focusing on the company's expanding monetisation opportunities.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 250 • DITP is expected to remain the key earnings engine, with monetisation driving growth. • Merchant expansion is expected to shift towards the long tail. • Affordability is expected to emerge as a key monetisation engine. • IAP is expected to develop into a recurring revenue stream.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 5,870 • Platform deliveries are improving across aircraft and helicopters. • Manufacturing activity is beginning to pick up across platforms. • Engine availability for the LCA Mk1A programme is improving as supply constraints ease. • Focus is shifting towards execution and conversion.

• Rating: Buy • Target price: Rs 6,175 • Execution is broadening across platforms. • Multiple handovers demonstrate improving breadth of execution. • Dhruv NG execution is progressing well and establishes a civil reference. • HTT-40 creates another scalable production stream despite execution delays.

• Rating: Outperform • Target price: Rs 5,481 • Expects the second half to be stronger for HAL. • HAL has received 10 GE F404-IN20 engines and expects to deliver 10 Tejas Mk-1A aircraft by March. • GE has committed to supplying another 12 engines by December. • HAL highlighted US$27 billion of business visibility.
Dolphin Offshore Enterprises and Max Estates have been removed from the ASM framework.
Rays of Belief has completed an overseas acquisition through its wholly owned subsidiary.
Mom's Belief US Inc acquired 100% of the equity shareholding of City Pro Group Inc for an aggregate consideration of $2 million.
The bank established a $500 million Medium-Term Note Programme.
Jaiprakash Power Ventures has reached an agreement with NARCL to settle claims linked to insolvency proceedings.
The company will pay Rs 511 crore as a full and final settlement, after which the IBC proceedings will be withdrawn.
Persistent Systems has moved closer to its proposed Nagarro acquisition, with shareholders set to consider a fresh equity raise in October.

The company said an EGM will be held in October 2026 to approve an equity raise of up to USD 450 million, while combined equity and borrowings will be capped at USD 1,250 million. The initial acceptance period ended on September 17, with the minimum acceptance threshold of 50% plus one share met.
Jaguar Land Rover has begun talks with global banks for a five-year loan of about $1.3 billion, The Economic Times reported.
Some lenders have sought clarity on N Chandrasekaran’s leadership at Tata Sons, though JLR said developments at its parent group do not directly affect its operations.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described talks with Chinese officials on artificial intelligence, trade and investment as “very successful”, Bloomberg reported.
The two sides agreed to establish a US-China dialogue on AI to discuss shared goals and threats. Officials are also preparing for a meeting between the US and Chinese presidents on Thursday.
Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.38%, while South Korea’s Kospi advanced 0.97%. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 declined 0.16%, while China’s Shanghai Composite was little changed.
Investors tracked higher US equity futures and the outlook for US-China trade ahead of a planned summit later this week.
GIFT Nifty traded at 23,338.50, indicating a subdued start for Indian equities with the Nifty 50 expected to open about 40 points lower.
